target_customer: Developers and small teams who want to run coding agents and open models locally for privacy and without per-token fees
problem: Running large open models locally needs tuned hardware and software, and cloud inference means ongoing token costs and sending code off site.
business_model: Hardware sales of a preconfigured inference workstation (Developer tier from $5,999) with an open source inference engine; business pricing quoted case by case
product_category: Local AI inference workstation and open source inference engine

founders.name: Alessandro Puppo
founders.background_notes: YC page tagline calls him a P25 alum. Notion and Cua per everydev.ai profile.

founders.name: Davide Cifarelli
previous_startups: Klara Labs (open source LLM interpretability project)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; CTO title per everydev.ai profile.

competitors.name: NVIDIA DGX Spark
competitors.what: Small desktop AI box for local inference

competitors.name: Framework Desktop and other Strix Halo mini PCs
competitors.what: AMD Ryzen AI Max mini PCs sold for local LLM inference, such as GMKtec EVO-X2 and Beelink GTR9 Pro
competitors.traction_then: Covered as best value for home LLMs in 2026 guides

technical_complexity.rationale: Assembling AMD hardware is routine, but a tuned open source inference engine with reported speedups over a DGX Spark and a llama.cpp fork needs real systems work. Speed claims are self-reported.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware is commodity AMD parts and the engine is open source, so the moat rests on software tuning, community and the planned self-improving layer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: NVIDIA sells DGX Spark and DGX Station and many mini PC vendors target local LLMs, but none were found copying the self-improving positioning.

market_need_then: Open models improved and Strix Halo class hardware made local inference practical in 2025 and 2026. Lucebox cites 2.9K GitHub stars and 95K+ Hugging Face downloads as demand signals (YC page, self-reported). Memory price increases raised hardware costs in 2026.

branding.domain_note: lucebox.com is used. GitHub organization is Luce-Org, labeled Lucebox AI.

identity.logo: Logo mark image, design not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise, short declarative headlines such as Intelligence you own; emphasizes ownership, privacy and speed

branding.community_and_virality: Open source engine with 70+ contributors and 920+ pull requests per the website; tech press covered the Zero 495 launch (Notebookcheck, Startup Fortune, 2026). Several articles are aggregator style.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press and open source traction in 2026, but no evidence yet of a brand driven pull beyond the product.

outcome_analysis: Lucebox is a Winter 2027 hardware and open source company with a two person team that opened direct orders for its Zero 495 workstation in September 2026. Its open source traction and AMD partnership are early positives, but the hardware is commodity and NVIDIA and mini PC makers compete, so the outcome is not yet known.
notes: everydev.ai lists investors as Y Combinator and Vento Ventures with no amounts; this is a single aggregator, so no round is recorded. Founding year conflicts (2025 on YC page, 2026 in some aggregators). Price figures vary across articles ($5,999 to $6,499). A PromptQuorum review relies on the company's own README. Founder education not found. The Luce prefix may be Italian for light but no source says so.
